# The History of the Bicycle

## An Idea Waiting for Its Materials

The bicycle is a curious object in the history of technology. It requires no fuel, no combustion, no electrical grid, and no exotic materials that were unavailable to the Romans or the Song dynasty. And yet it appears astonishingly late — the first recognizable ancestor of the bicycle rolls onto the roads of Europe only in 1817, a full decade after the steamboat and a century after the Newcomen engine. Historians have puzzled over this gap. The likeliest answer is that the bicycle is not one invention but a stack of them: precision metal bearings, drawn wire, vulcanized rubber, chain drive, and above all the machine-tool infrastructure to make thousands of identical small parts cheaply.
